DDB_READ_RATIO.label: [Assumed]
DDB_READ_RATIO.source: fraction of events that trigger a personalisation lookup

DDB_STORAGE_GB.label: [Assumed]
DDB_STORAGE_GB.source: visitor profile store across 500 tenants, steady state

DDB_WRITES_PER_EVENT.label: [Assumed]
DDB_WRITES_PER_EVENT.source: naive model: one visitor-profile update per event. See WRITE AMPLIFICATION in the output - this is the single most expensive assumption in the model

ELASTICACHE_NODES.label: [Assumed]
ELASTICACHE_NODES.source: primary plus one replica for failover

ELASTICACHE_R7G_LARGE_HOUR.label: [Benchmarked]
ELASTICACHE_R7G_LARGE_HOUR.source: aws.amazon.com/elasticache/pricing/ cache.r7g.large - taken from a worked example on the page, not from a rate table; confirm before committing budget

FLINK_KPUS.label: [Assumed]
FLINK_KPUS.source: 1 KPU = 1 vCPU + 4GB. Throughput per KPU is entirely job-dependent and this is the least defensible number in the model. Sensitivity is reported below

HEADROOM.label: [Assumed]
HEADROOM.source: provision 30% above the modelled peak so a spike does not land exactly at capacity; the alternative is discovering the ceiling during Black Friday

KINESIS_RECORDS_PER_SHARD.label: [Benchmarked]
KINESIS_RECORDS_PER_SHARD.source: aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-streams/pricing/: 'One shard provides an ingest capacity of 1 MB/second or 1,000 records/second'

LAKE_MONTHS.label: [Assumed]
LAKE_MONTHS.source: S3 cost shown at end of year one, when it is largest

MEAN_EVENT_BYTES.label: [Observed]
MEAN_EVENT_BYTES.source: measured over fixtures/event_sample.jsonl: 25 events, mean 229B, median 228B, range 200-285B

PARQUET_COMPRESSION.label: [Assumed]
PARQUET_COMPRESSION.source: columnar Parquet with Snappy over highly repetitive JSON event data; unverified for this payload shape and worth measuring in week one

S3_FLUSH_SECONDS.label: [Assumed]
S3_FLUSH_SECONDS.source: how often the stream job writes a file to S3; trades object count against freshness of the lake, and does not affect dashboard latency
